name: Omni compliance playbook
source: Omni best-practice framework for US prescription-drug promotion. Guidance, not legal advice: the company's SOPs and MLR decide.

review_cycle.what: Objective, audience, channel and the references every claim will rest on.
Every claim linked to the exact page and line of its reference.
Is it accurate, current and supported by the evidence?
Claims, risk wording, rights to images and music, contests and offers.
Consistent with the label, fair balance, ISI and PI; whether Form FDA 2253 is needed.
Approved version locked with a job code and an expiry date.
Promotional pieces sent to FDA's Office of Prescription Drug Promotion at first use.
Re-review at expiry or when the label changes; pull every copy everywhere when withdrawn.

claims.detail: Every claim matches the approved indication, population and dosing. No off-label use in promotion.
Efficacy claims rest on adequate, well-controlled evidence, cited to the page.
Risks get prominence and readability comparable to benefits, in the same piece.
Important safety information visible or one click away on every asset; prescribing information linked.
No 'safe', 'cure' or 'no side effects'; no burying or softening of risks.
Superiority or comparative claims only with direct comparative evidence.
Unsolicited off-label questions go to Medical Information, not the rep or the brand team.
Consumer pieces use plain language and keep the risk information understandable.

channels.name: Rep visit (face to face)
rules: Approved detail aids and leave-behinds only
Meals and items of value follow the PhRMA Code and are reported under Open Payments
Off-label questions referred to Medical Information
channels.refs: PhRMA Code · Sunshine Act · Anti-Kickback Statute

channels.name: Rep-triggered email
rules: Approved templates; reps choose, never edit
Sent only to HCPs who opted in
ISI and PI link in every email

channels.name: Brand email (HQ)
rules: Documented opt-in and a working unsubscribe
Opt-outs honoured within 10 business days
Frequency caps shared with rep email

channels.name: Webinars & speaker programs
rules: Speakers trained and use approved slides
Fair-market-value fees; attendee meals within PhRMA limits
Off-label questions answered by Medical, not the speaker
channels.refs: PhRMA Code · OIG guidance on speaker programs · Sunshine Act

channels.name: Congresses & medical meetings
rules: Promotional booth separate from medical (non-promotional) activity
Only approved materials on the booth
Country rules apply at international meetings

channels.name: Display, programmatic & endemic
rules: Benefit and risk balanced within the ad, or a prominent link to risk information
HCP-only content shown only to verified HCPs
Keep a record of every live creative and placement
channels.refs: 21 CFR 202.1 · FDA guidance on space-limited media

channels.name: Paid search
rules: Branded ads that name a benefit need risk information or a direct path to it
Avoid naming the condition and brand together without balance
Pre-approve keyword lists
channels.refs: FDA untitled letters on search ads

channels.name: Paid & organic social
rules: Benefit and risk together where space allows; otherwise link to full risk
Comments moderated; adverse events reported
Influencers disclose they are paid and use approved claims only
channels.refs: FDA social-media draft guidance · FTC endorsement guides

channels.name: TV & connected TV
rules: Major statement of risks in audio and text, clear and neutral
Adequate provision: where to find full prescribing information
Submit to OPDP; consider advisory review before first airing

channels.name: Patient website
rules: ISI on every page; full PI and Medication Guide linked
Plain language
Forms collect only what's needed, with consent

channels.name: Patient CRM (email & SMS)
rules: Prior express written consent for marketing texts
Health data handled as sensitive; consent kept on record
Easy opt-out in every message

channels.name: Patient support & hub
rules: HIPAA authorisation before using patient data for marketing
Copay help excludes government-insured patients
Nurse educators don't promote or give medical advice beyond the label

channels.name: EHR / point of care
rules: Messages don't interfere with clinical decision-making
Vendor and EHR rules on sponsored content apply
Clearly marked as sponsored

channels.name: Medical science liaisons
rules: Non-promotional: scientific exchange only
Off-label discussion only in response to unsolicited questions
No sales targets or call plans shared with sales

data_privacy.detail: Capture when and how each person agreed to be contacted, per channel.
Unsubscribes flow to every channel and vendor; email within 10 business days at most (CAN-SPAM).
Marketing SMS only with prior express written consent (TCPA).
Data from providers or pharmacies needs a HIPAA authorisation before marketing use.
Consumer health data falls under state laws such as CCPA/CPRA and Washington's My Health My Data Act.
Meals, fees and travel for HCPs are tracked and reported to CMS Open Payments.

adverse_events.detail: An adverse event or product complaint seen anywhere goes to pharmacovigilance, typically within one business day (company SOP sets the clock).
Brand social pages, comment sections and chat are monitored on a set schedule.
Agencies, call centres and hub staff complete AE-reporting training before go-live.
Decide which sources are monitored; whatever is monitored must be reviewed for AEs.

regulations.name: FD&C Act · 21 CFR 202.1
regulations.what: Prescription-drug advertising: consistent with the label, fair balance, brief summary.

regulations.name: Form FDA 2253 · 21 CFR 314.81
regulations.what: Promotional materials submitted to FDA at first use.

regulations.name: FDA OPDP
regulations.what: Office of Prescription Drug Promotion: reviews promotion, issues untitled and warning letters.

regulations.name: PhRMA Code
regulations.what: Voluntary code for interactions with HCPs: meals, speaker programs, items of value.

regulations.name: Anti-Kickback Statute
regulations.what: No payment or item of value to induce prescribing of federally reimbursed drugs.

regulations.name: Sunshine Act · Open Payments
regulations.what: Transfers of value to HCPs and teaching hospitals reported to CMS.

regulations.name: HIPAA
regulations.what: Protected health information from covered entities; authorisation for marketing use.

regulations.name: CAN-SPAM Act
regulations.what: Commercial email: honest headers, a working opt-out, honoured fast.

regulations.name: TCPA
regulations.what: Consent for marketing calls and texts.
